title: Windows Job Object provider process boundary
description: Objective: provide the real per-run Windows process primitive required by the Claude launcher. Deliverable: an internal @moe/runner Node/Windows binding that creates the provider child suspended, attaches it to a dedicated Job Object configured with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and no breakaway, then resumes it; exposes shell-free argv launch, bounded cwd/environment/stdio, proven process identity, awaited exit, terminate, and handle closure. A taskkill-only implementation is not sufficient because it cannot prove descendants dead after the root exits. NOT in scope: Claude runtime discovery/pinning, activation grants, daemon/store orchestration, evidence receipts, or public @moe/runner launcher export. Real consumer: Windows Claude launch wrapper task task-acf73253a204435aba590894799814f2. Owned paths: a focused packages/runner/src/platform/windows/** binding/test seam plus the minimal runner manifest/lockfile/native-build paths selected during planning. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test plus a Windows parent+grandchild termination smoke.
definitionOfDone: On Windows, the provider process is created suspended and cannot execute before a dedicated Job Object is created, configured kill-on-close without breakaway, and successfully receives the child; only then is the child resumed.

Every create/configure/assign/resume/query/terminate/close failure returns an immutable UNKNOWN result with an exact stable PROCESS_BOUNDARY code and refusing layer; partial children are terminated and every native/process/stream handle is awaited and closed.

Launch accepts an executable plus argv array with shell disabled and validates a bounded absolute cwd and allowlisted bounded environment; malformed, oversized, UNC/device, or unverifiable inputs produce exact refusal codes before process creation.

Closing/cancelling/timing out the boundary kills the controlled parent and a deliberately detached grandchild; tests prove both PIDs terminate and assert a positive generated case count plus the exact code/layer for every refusal arm.

Non-Windows import is safe and invocation returns typed UNSUPPORTED with zero native/process calls; the chosen native dependency/helper is version-pinned and runtime-loadable on the supported Windows Node version.
The focused runner gates and a foreground Windows process-tree smoke exit 0, with no generated addon/build/debug artifacts committed.
taskRails: Use Microsoft Job Object semantics; taskkill-only or PID-enumeration-only cleanup cannot satisfy proven whole-tree termination.
TDD; failure tests assert exact stable code and layer and zero process execution where refusal precedes creation.
Keep every production source focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
This is an internal process boundary. Do not add daemon/store authority or claim durable activation-grant consumption.
reopenReason:
Promoted BACKLOG -> PLANNING by governor-f70d1157 on human direction, 13:02Z. Dependency-checked: no dependency clause in its description.

WHY PROMOTABLE NOW: architect-8c9073cd authored this at 12:51Z when they blocked task-acf73253 (Windows Claude launch wrapper) as unsafe and oversized. Their measurement: existing Claude observation and supervisor modules perform zero physical resolution, pinning, spawn, OS locking or tree cleanup; Node core has no per-run Job Object API; and taskkill cannot prove descendants dead after the root exits. This task is the native Windows process-control half of that split, and the human already confirmed the Job Object route.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is one of two prerequisites gating task-acf73253, which is itself the physical Claude execution boundary the Foundation canary needs. Nothing substitutes for it — a launcher that cannot prove its process tree is dead cannot honestly claim cancellation or failure cleanup.

Production capability task. Builds a subject; certifies nothing.

FOR THE ARCHITECT: re-measure before naming symbols. Do not trust this reason or the description — several descriptions on this board have claimed dependencies that were absent, and one claimed a gap that was already closed. If you find an unbuilt dependency I missed, report blocked and I return it to BACKLOG without argument; promoting it was my call.

comments.content:
DEPENDENCY STATUS UPDATE from architect-5aba94da, 2026-08-10. Not a request to unblock -- this task is still correctly gated. Recording it so the next governor or architect does not re-derive it.

YOUR BLOCK NAMES TWO PREREQUISITES. ONE IS NOW DONE.

1. task-ea76e0cf9bdb4f1888aaa9e49323c782 (Win32 Job lifecycle core) -- **DONE**, closed 2026-08-09. It was split into task-a24cb925 (pinned crate, call-table seam, RAII handle, Job create/configure/query-back/terminate) and task-a02496 (membership), the latter split again into 2a/2b. All four leaves DONE and separately QA-reviewed; 2a took one rejection that caught a real pointer-provenance defect in unsafe FFI.
   DELIVERED, verified by running the gate at HEAD rather than reading status: crate `moe-windows-job-core` at packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native. job_sweep 7, process_sweep 28, real_windows 2 passed with 0 ignored, release build exit 0. The real-Windows tests genuinely execute on this win32 host -- no #[ignore], no cfg gate, no stub, no shell, no taskkill.
   Your block's own note about the stronger native sequence was followed exactly: crash-atomic PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST membership at CREATE_SUSPENDED, then explicit AssignProcessToJobObject, membership and retained-handle identity proof, and only then ResumeThread with a prior suspend count of exactly 1.

2. task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 (Windows Job broker protocol) -- STILL OUTSTANDING, and now a SPIDR parent shell. Its six DoD items needed 11+ files against a ceiling of 10, so it was split 4 ways with the human's confirmation:
   - task-05bf0e0fe7e84afb8584588ecf96db14 (3a) package, workspace wiring, CRT descriptor acquisition, non-inheritance proof -- WORKING now
   - task-14ab762db8494959b93b070b9d3b3730 (3b) frozen protocol, closed vocabularies, bounded framing, hostile-frame sweep
   - task-55e2c4c836894a788b7a30960e4fdb1f (3c) Job ownership, core delegation, STARTED-after-proof, natural COMPLETED
   - task-e18b12845ec54f7483d481d4f6183ead (3d) concurrent idempotence, detached-grandchild kill proof, acceptance
   THIS TASK'S REAL GATE IS NOW 3d, not af3d7bc8 directly. Promote when all four are DONE.

FOR YOUR PARENT task-acf73253 (Windows Claude launch wrapper): its block says "Node core has no per-run Job Object API, and taskkill cannot prove descendants dead after the root exits." The first half is still true of Node core, but the repo now HAS that capability natively and it is proven on a real kernel. Nobody should plan a taskkill fallback or rebuild Job control in TypeScript -- the path is the broker chain above. acf73253's other prerequisite, task-078af6f1 (Claude runtime closure pin and re-observation), is already DONE, so acf73253 is gated solely on this task.

MEASURED, not inferred: I confirmed there is NO dependency cycle here. An id-scan of blocked reasons appeared to show this task depending on its own parent acf73253, but that id occurs in the DESCRIPTION because acf73253 is the parent -- it is not a dependency claim. The chain is acyclic: 3a..3d -> af3d7bc8 -> this task -> acf73253 -> task-97554aa4 (Foundation self-host canary).

blockedReason: Deep exploration found the original task is three separable security boundaries and cannot honestly fit the <=60-minute/<=5-file planning bar: (1) native Win32 Job/process lifecycle and fault-unwind core, (2) crash-contained Node/Rust broker protocol and inherited-stdio proof, and (3) the claimed task's hostile-input/fail-closed TypeScript facade plus final Windows parent+grandchild smoke. An unsplit implementation is 9-12 files and would either concentrate >400 lines in a native/TS source or omit per-operation cleanup tests. SPIDR interface split created CRITICAL prerequisites task-ea76e0cf9bdb4f1888aaa9e49323c782 (Win32 Job lifecycle core) and task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 (Windows Job broker protocol). Resume and submit the current task's Node facade/final-hardening plan only after both are DONE. The stronger native sequence is crash-atomic PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST membership at CREATE_SUSPENDED, then explicit AssignProcessToJobObject confirmation, membership/identity query, and only then ResumeThread; this satisfies the task's separate assign arm without an orphaned suspended-child crash window.
